newsitem.title: INDIA: Coal India expects $1.05 bln soft loan.
newsitem.headline: Coal India expects $1.05 bln soft loan.

text.p: State-owned Coal India Ltd (CIL) said on Thursday that it expects the World Bank and the Export-Import Bank of Japan to grant it a $1.05 billion concessional loan for its rehabilitation programme.
A senior CIL official told Reuters that the final round of negotiations between CIL, the World Bank and Japan's Exim bank was expected to take place next month.
"The World Bank board is expected to ratify the loan approval by the end of June this year," the CIL official said, without divulging the details of the loan.
He said the Coal Sector Rehabilitation Programme (CSRP) would cost an estimated $1.8 billion and cover 25 mining projects.
The programme aims at substantially raising coal output at CIL, a monopoly producer in India.
"Three of the 25 mining projects are new and the rest are for modernisation and expansion of the existing mines," the official said.
The CIL has already approached the government to treat the CSRP as a single project for import duty benefit, company officials said.
Officials said the restructuring was expected to be completed within five years. The loan would be repaid with 15 years of completion of the rehabilitation programme.
They said the success of CIL's $90 million Environment and Social Mitigation Programme (ESMP) would be one of the preconditions for the CSRP loan.
The World Bank has already sanctioned $63 million for the ESMP, he added.
